segments: When you have multiple NixOS nodes, such as a primary computer, a server, and a Raspberry Pi, running nixos-rebuild switch on each is cumbersome and makes version drift more likely. Colmena lets you push configuration to all nodes centrally from your primary computer.

The following is a traditional hive.nix example using the locally selected Nixpkgs; production projects should pin a Nixpkgs revision. When using a Flake, export colmena / colmenaHive as required by your Colmena version. Do not put an unbound inputs variable directly into a standalone file.
Push and activate: colmena apply switch --on server (omitting the node filter may deploy to multiple nodes)

Build locally, install remotely: after building, you can copy the system closure. Building an ARM system on x86_64 requires proper cross-compilation, emulation, or a remote builder; simply copying binaries is not enough. You can also use deployment.buildOnTarget to build on the target node.
Parallel deployment: upgrade 10 servers at once to exactly the same version.

Fault tolerance: older NixOS generations provide a recovery path, but Colmena does not guarantee automatic network recovery or rollback after every failure. Prepare SSH connectivity checks, a console channel, and manual recovery procedures before deployment.

If you previously used Ansible to manage multiple Arch machines, think of Colmena as a tool that coordinates building, copying, and activation on top of NixOS's declarative system configuration. Mutable application state still needs separate management.
Boundaries Between Building, Previewing, and Activation

build normally only builds; with buildOnTarget enabled, the result resides on the target machine. dry-activate may first build, transfer the closure, and run the target's preview script, so it is not a purely local, read-only check. test activates immediately without making the configuration the boot default; boot changes the boot default without activating immediately; switch does both. The example hostnames are placeholders. Deploy only after confirming the target, authorized account, and hardware configuration.
